A comprehensive overview of quadratic equations, including quadratic trinomials, completing the square,
    the discriminant, Vieta's formulas, factoring, real-life applications, and even methods for solving them mentally.
Before solving quadratic equations, you must be able to solve elementary ones. There is no other way. Don't even try.
Huge collection of word problems which lead to an equations with detailed solutions.
An open and free online collection of mathematics educational materials.
A large amount of materials and many typical practice problems.

Learn how quadratic equations arise from real-life situations,
    what quadratic equations and quadratic trinomials are,
    how they are related, and how to determine whether an equation is quadratic.

Examples of various real-life situations that boil down to quadratic equations.
          This will make it clear why we need to be able to solve them at all.

Polynomial with the maximum power of the variable equal to two.
          Acts as a "template" or "general form" for all quadratic equations.
Any equation that can be reduced to the form of a quadratic trinomial by transformations without losing roots.

Quadratic equations with missing terms (incomplete quadratics) are the simplest forms of quadratic equations where the coefficient B, C, or both are missing.
    Let's learn how to solve them correctly in each specific case.
What is an incomplete quadratic equation?
A quadratic equation in which coefficient B or C or both are zero.
How to solve incomplete quadratic equations?
Detailed analysis of solving all types of incomplete quadratic equations with derivation of general formulas.
General formulas for incomplete quadratic equations
General formulas for solving incomplete quadratic equations

Formulas for all three types of incomplete quadratic equations:
          when "B" and "C" are zero, when "C" is zero, and when "B" is zero.

The technique of "packing" an expanded expression into a compact squared binomial.
    This method allows you to solve any quadratic equation!
    Let's learn how to do it with detailed examples and visualizations.
"Packing" an expanded expression into a squared binomial.
Completing the square is a powerful tool for transforming expressions and solving quadratic equations.
Solving quadratic equations by completing the square
Completing the square is the key to solving absolutely any quadratic equations.
How a large square is literally assembled or "completed" from smaller shapes.

A clear derivation of the quadratic formula with a detailed explanation of every step.
    Learn what the discriminant is, where it comes from, and how it tells you how many roots a quadratic equation has.
What is a general formula for equation roots?
General root formulas let you solve a whole class of equations by direct substitution.
What is the discriminant of a quadratic equation?
A special number computed from the coefficients of a quadratic equation. It tells you how many roots the equation has.
A general formula that lets you find the roots of any quadratic equation by plugging in the coefficients.
A special type of fourth-degree equation that you can solve by reducing it to a quadratic equation.
Why there is no general formula for degree 5+
For equations above the 4th degree, there is no universal "plug in numbers -- get roots" formula.
How to solve a quadratic equation
A diagram that shows how to solve any quadratic equation step by step.
How to derive the quadratic formula
A step-by-step derivation of the quadratic formula with explanations.
Quadratic equation with even B coefficient
A simpler root formula for quadratics when the coefficient B is even.
Sridhara method for deriving the quadratic formula
A faster way to derive the quadratic formula, with one small trick.
Definition of trinomial equations and worked examples of solving them by reducing to a quadratic equation.
A special kind of equation with three terms, where the same "unknown function" appears in different powers and the whole thing can be reduced to a quadratic.
Definition of reciprocal (palindromic) equations and worked examples solved by reducing them to quadratic equations.
A special kind of equation where coefficients mirror each other around the equation's "center".

Rewriting quadratic trinomials and quadratic equations as a product of factors instead of a sum of terms.
    Lets you solve equations quickly, simplify messy expressions, and spot the roots immediately.
In different situations, you need to be able to write expressions both as sums and as products of factors.
Why is factoring a quadratic trinomial useful?
Factoring quadratic trinomials lets you simplify expressions, see the roots right away, and gives you an alternative way to solve quadratic equations.
A method for factoring "simple" quadratic trinomials by hand.
Formula for factoring a quadratic trinomial
If a quadratic trinomial has roots, it can always be factored using those roots.
Any two numbers can be roots!
Any pair of numbers can be the roots of a quadratic trinomial
The general factorization formula implies that any two numbers are roots of some quadratic trinomial.
Coordinate plane of roots of quadratic equations
A geometric visualization of the fact that absolutely any two numbers can be roots of some quadratic trinomial.
All possible ways a quadratic trinomial can factor.
Deriving the factorization formula for a quadratic trinomial
A step-by-step derivation of the factorization formula for a quadratic trinomial, with notes.
Exercises for practicing factoring biquadratic trinomials through an intermediate substitution.

Two simple and very useful formulas that connect the roots of a quadratic trinomial with its coefficients.
    They let you check roots quickly, build equations, and study special kinds of quadratic equations.

The sum of the roots of a quadratic trinomial equals -B/A, and the product of the roots equals C/A.
          There are no numbers other than the roots that satisfy these formulas.
Is it Vieta's formulas or Vieta's theorem?

In English, "Vieta's formulas" is the usual name, though some books also say "Vieta's theorem."
              This topic uses "Vieta's formulas" as the main name.
How do you remember Vieta's formulas?
You do not have to memorize them; they are derived instantly by expanding the brackets in the factored form.
What are Vieta's formulas used for?
The formulas are used for quick root checks, building equations from roots, and establishing links between coefficients.

It is enough to write the equality between the standard quadratic trinomial form and its factorized form.
          Then just expand the brackets.

A detailed breakdown of every way to solve quadratic equations mentally.
    Includes infinitely generated practice problems for each method separately and for all methods mixed together.

Every incomplete quadratic equation can be solved mentally by one of three formulas.
          There is nothing to guess.
          The solution is straightforward.
Mental solving of quadratic equations from the sum of coefficients

A zero sum of coefficients lets you get the roots instantly.
          This is the simplest and most useful way to solve quadratic equations mentally.
Mental solving of quadratic equations through a perfect square

Sometimes a quadratic equation can be packed entirely into a square of a sum or a difference.
          In that case it has one root, and that root is easy to get.
Mental solving of quadratic equations by factoring

If the quadratic equation is monic (A = 1), you can try factoring it mentally.
          Find t and k so that t + k = B and tk = C. Then the roots are -t and -k.
How do you get a monic quadratic equation?

A simple way to turn a quadratic equation into a monic one that may be solvable mentally.
          To do it, transfer coefficient A to C.
Ways to solve quadratic equations mentally

A convenient chart listing all fast ways to solve quadratic equations mentally.
          Includes hints about the roots.
Practice problems on mentally solving quadratic equations

Infinitely generated practice on all methods of mental solving of quadratic equations:
          zero sum, perfect square, factoring, and transferring A to C.
